description:
## Goal

Make `PatternDispatchPlan` outcome bindings the sole authority for values a successful inline pattern arm receives. Delete the second bind-only syntax walk that independently reconstructs tuple, list, map, struct, and bitstring projections after dispatch.

## Proven failure and boundary

The production program `metadata() -> %{__fz_local__: 42}; case metadata() do %{__fz_span__: _} -> 0; _ -> 42 end` returns 42 through the interpreter but JIT/AOT fail when native lowering tries to materialize an Absent value. Fresh-base telemetry shows the open map type conservatively retains both runtime arms; this is not a bad reachability decision. The contradiction begins later: the authoritative pattern plan records no outcome binding for wildcard `_`, while `lower_match_clause_block -> bind_pattern -> lower_map_pattern(with_asserts=false)` re-walks the source pattern and emits `RequireMapValue` for every field anyway. RuntimeDemand correctly marks that unused projection `Ignore`/`Nothing`; backend/native still receive the redundant instruction.

This ticket owns the inline dispatch-outcome-to-arm-binding seam. It is blocked by `fz-kdt.27`, because a struct outcome cannot be trusted until the plan carries a typed named-struct discriminator and exact named-field subjects. It consumes that model after `.27` closes. Function-clause heads remain the distinct `fz-5xp.56` cutover; they are not an inline control arm and do not block this ticket.

Inspect and reuse the existing `PatternDispatchPlan.outcomes.bindings`, `PatternSubjectRef`, interpreter/receive subject resolution, inline control-entry parameters, and plan ordering before changing code. The graph remains the sole test/project authority: map value projection is legal only on the key-present edge. Standalone asserting matches and function-clause heads may retain their current lowering until their actual consumers are cut over, but successful inline arms must not reconstruct plan decisions from syntax.

## Correct model

A pattern plan has one output contract per winning row: its ordered bindings name only source variables/aliases and the exact `PatternSubjectRef` that supplies each value. Wildcards and literal-only subpatterns contribute no binding and therefore no arm parameter, projection instruction, runtime demand, transport lane, or native work. A bound nested value is projected exactly once from the plan-owned subject path after the winning branch established its prerequisites.

Inline `case`, `with`, and `with else` arm environments consume those plan-owned bindings using the same subject/projection vocabulary already used by receive/interpreter execution. Each arm has its own ordered parameter contract; arms need not bind the same names or number of values. Semantic analysis derives each parameter type from the same plan subject under that winning rows refined inputs. Map and struct subjects retain exact field lookup types; bitstring subjects retain field-kind types rather than widening to `any`.

Preserve exact source-order outcome selection and contextual variable identity. Do not special-case map wildcards, infer bindings from rendered names, re-walk `Pattern`, or retain both plan bindings and syntax bindings as inline authorities.

## TDD signal

Pin the standalone reproduction through interpreter, JIT, and AOT: all return 42. Authoritative backend/IR/telemetry proves the wildcard map arm contributes no `RequireMapValue`, runtime lane, materialization, or native work. Add controls where `%{key: value}` binds `value` and where nested tuple/list/map/struct/bitstring variables require exact plan-owned projections; repeated/as-pattern bindings preserve their established diagnostics and values. Cover arms with different binding arities, captures shadowed by pattern bindings, present `nil` versus absent keys, dependent bitstring sizes, `case`, `with`, and `with else`, source/clause order, and allocation/read counts.

The struct controls consume the completed `fz-kdt.27` contract: typed named-struct discrimination and exact field subjects already exist before this ticket routes those bindings into inline arms. Function-head duplicate bitstring reads remain owned by `fz-5xp.56`; inline bitstring fields must nevertheless be transported from the existing dispatch extraction exactly once.

Prove the result at the production boundary used by fz-tfn.62: source-less quoted metadata may carry typed syntax metadata without fabricated span metadata, and its impossible-at-runtime span arm passes every execution door. Preserve exact diagnostics for malformed patterns and genuinely missing required keys, all existing dispatch behavior, deterministic artifacts, and causal work counts.

## Strategy and deletion

Give each inline arm explicit parameters in its plan-outcome binding order, install those names into the arm environment, and resolve the corresponding subject values from branch evidence only after that outcome wins. Reuse the interpreter dispatch match result, native `DispatchState`, control-entry parameter machinery, semantic branch parameter input, and existing backend packaging. Do not add a second transport model.

Delete the bind-only work from `lower_match_clause_block` and `lower_match_success_block`. Retain `bind_pattern` only for its proven function-head consumer until `fz-5xp.56`; retain `apply_pattern` only for genuine standalone asserting matches. Remove redundant projection steps and downstream demand/transport work rather than padding them.

Do not patch `env_runtime_var`, widen RuntimeDemand, synthesize placeholders, retain impossible/unused lanes, add a native-only exception, second resolver/store/scanner, display-string identity, or compatibility path. Update pattern/dispatch documentation to state the single inline binding authority and the explicit function-head remainder. Run focused RED-to-GREEN, library, fixture, CLI, AOT, formatting, check, strict Clippy, deterministic work/allocation gates, and a fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review. One ticket, one commit, one close; no construction debris.

## User-guide handoff

The user guide currently claims every pattern is destructured once. When this ticket closes, that statement may be made exact for inline case/with/with-else arms only. State the remaining function-clause-head duplication plainly and point to fz-5xp.56; do not preserve a universal claim until that ticket removes the final second lowering.
title: Make inline dispatch outcome bindings the sole pattern-projection authority
